FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_001  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` only iterates over `responses.items()` for failure detection and failure-history recording. Any active model that was allocated work but never returned a response is silently ignored: no EMPTY/TIMEOUT failure is detected, no failure history is recorded, the model remains active, and role reassignment/future allocation proceeds as if the model simply did not exist this round. This is a cross-cutting orchestration bug because Area 2 allocates work by model, Area 6 failure handling expects per-model response assessment, and Area 1 reassignment uses recorded failures. The missing-model case is operationally equivalent to a severe transport failure and should be synthesized explicitly from the allocation or expected active model set.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes convergence and diminishing-returns metrics from the entire `findings` list before filtering out findings emitted by failed, excluded, or non-responding models. As a result, a model can both fail at the transport/protocol layer and still contribute findings that increase `kappa`, increase yield, and influence stop decisions in the same round. This violates the intended separation between valid round outputs and failure handling, and creates a cross-area inconsistency: Area 6 can declare output malformed while Areas 4–5 still consume its findings as evidence. Findings should be admitted only from responses that passed the relevant validity gates.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_003  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 2 (interface)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` accepts a `tasks` argument but never uses it, and `RoundResult.allocation` is always stored as `None`. This breaks the orchestrator contract needed for cross-area validation: the manager cannot verify that every allocated model responded, cannot tie failures to assigned tasks, cannot use `check_reallocation_depth(task_id)`, and cannot reconstruct which missing outputs should count as failures. The omission is deeper than a cosmetic unused parameter: it disconnects Area 2 allocation from Area 6 recovery and makes the top-level orchestration incapable of enforcing task-level management semantics.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_004  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` records exclusions by removing models from `_active_models`, but downgrade/degrade-style recoveries (`DOWNGRADE_ROLE`, `DEGRADE`) have no state effect anywhere in the system. `DynamicManager.process_round()` does not interpret these actions, emit corresponding recovery events, alter role assignment, or alter future allocation constraints. In practice, most non-fatal recovery policies are inert bookkeeping only. This is a cross-cutting execution gap between Area 6 policy selection and Areas 1–2 orchestration: the code decides a recovery action but does not apply it.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_005  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 4 (completeness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: The “real-time manager monitoring interface” is only partially wired. `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits some failure events, but `get_recovery()` does not emit recovery events such as `RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, or `ABORT`, and `DynamicManager.process_round()` never emits `MODEL_RESPONSE` or `ROUND_START` despite those event types being defined. This means the monitoring interface cannot observe key state transitions needed for live PM control. The gap spans the event schema, failure policy execution, and orchestration layer.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_006  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` and `LoadBalancer`/`Allocation` implicitly assume `model_id` and `task_id` uniqueness, but the module never validates uniqueness. Duplicate `model_id`s collapse in dict-based structures (`role_map`, `_model_idx`, `self.models` in `FailureHandler`), while duplicate `task_id`s break allocation lookup semantics and per-task load accounting. Because many core data structures are keyed by these IDs, duplicates can silently alias distinct entities and corrupt role assignment, failure tracking, and allocation retrieval without immediate exceptions.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_007  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array()` can produce negative or >1 components because it divides raw values by `pool_max` without validating the fingerprint domain. If any fingerprint field is negative, or if `D_decay` exceeds the pool maximum assumptions due to malformed input, the resulting normalized vector can fall outside [0,1], invalidating the documented interpretation of capability scores as bounded suitability values. Since configuration validation does not validate fingerprint values and `ModelSpec` has no post-init checks, role assignment can operate on nonsensical capability vectors.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_008  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` allows arbitrary `duration` values, including zero or negative numbers. `kappa_rate()` then computes `len(classes) / max(dt, 1e-10)`, so a negative duration is silently coerced into an enormous effective finding rate rather than rejected as invalid data. This can drive the rate metric sharply negative and destabilize convergence decisions from malformed telemetry instead of surfacing an input error.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_009  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` appends to `_perf_history` on every call, even for duplicate evaluations of the same model/round. If the orchestrator retries parsing or re-checks the same `ModelResponse`, underperformance persistence is artificially accelerated because history is keyed only by model, not by unique round/attempt identity. This can trigger `UNDERPERFORM` based on duplicate bookkeeping rather than distinct rounds.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_010  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 4 (completeness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: The correlated failure model is never integrated into dispatch, allocation, redundancy, abort policy, or convergence logic. The system computes correlation risk as a side utility only, but no decision path consumes it. This is a deeper cross-cutting omission than the already-noted formula issues: even if the probability formulas were correct, the management layer would remain behaviorally unchanged, so the “Area 6 extension” does not actually extend system behavior.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_011  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 1 (logic)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEventStream.emit()` invokes the external callback synchronously with no exception handling. A callback exception will propagate back into failure detection, feasibility checks, or round processing and can abort core management logic merely because monitoring code failed. Since the event stream is described as monitoring infrastructure, letting observer failures take down the controller is a control-plane/data-plane coupling flaw.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_012  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 6 (edge-case)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.solve()` permits construction with zero models when `tasks` is empty, returning an allocation with shape `(0, 0)` and no error. But `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` separately forbids zero active models. This inconsistency means the lower-level allocator treats an empty model pool as acceptable in one edge case while the orchestrator treats it as fatal. The contract for `K=0` is undefined and inconsistent across layers, which is a common source of latent integration bugs.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_013  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 5 (correctness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` sorts only by cached numeric score and does not apply the documented deterministic tie-break rule used in assignment. For tied scores, ordering falls back to dict insertion order rather than the specified `(A, v_bar, 1-D_decay, C)` lexicographic key. Any downstream consumer using `get_ordering()` as the public representation of `≽_rho` can observe an ordering inconsistent with actual assignment semantics.

FINDING_ID: F_MISSED_014  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 4 (completeness)  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` validates the `alpha_*` vectors but does not validate the analogous `b_pm`, `b_col`, `b_par` baseline vectors that drive expected-performance and underperformance detection. Wrong shape, negative values, or wildly scaled baselines can silently distort Area 6 behavior even though these coefficients are just as structurally important as the alpha vectors.
